director.chapterArc: Sleep-starved expectation of gentleness is broken by Rook’s severe drill; Dessa’s quiet spatial awareness is tested, confirmed, and named Ember; Ott’s intelligence turns discovery into a five-day tactical deadline; Rook publicly weighs pursuit against Senna’s survival and chooses the road; Senna’s early collapse forces him to spend his remaining ash and transfer responsibility to the younger four; at dawn, Toren and Rook sit with the cost of that choice while Toren withholds his own final disclosure.
director.restraintNote: Keep Original Calder measured, observant, and physically grounded. Treat magic as practical fact, calculations as emotional action, and sacrifice without nobility or uplift. Temporary color should remain narrow: dry humor, contained dread, unsentimental care, and grief expressed through arithmetic, objects, and silence.

cues.delivery: Let Milo’s enormous betrayal land as dry observational comedy, affectionate but entirely straight-faced.
cues.from: Milo looked after him with an expression of enormous betrayal.
cues.through: "He's exactly the same," he said.
cues.reason: A brief comic release sharpens the contrast with Dessa’s more serious correction.

cues.delivery: Barely disturb the air; the emptied voice is a summons made alarming by its lack of display.
cues.from: "Rook."
cues.through: "Rook."
cues.reason: Dessa’s single word initiates the chapter’s first major reversal.

cues.delivery: Inventory every position with practical precision while allowing contained disbelief to emerge only as the list proves impossible.
cues.from: "Milo's behind the cart," said Dessa. "He's at the off-side wheel, and he's crouched down doing the strap, and he's got the mug in his other hand. Wyck's at eleven paces, straight up the slope, standing still. The mule's — the mule's further than I thought. The mule's at about twenty-six, and it's eating. Senna's in the cart, and she's sat up. Tor's at the tailgate, and he's turned round now. He's turned round because I said your name."
cues.through: "Milo's behind the cart," said Dessa. "He's at the off-side wheel, and he's crouched down doing the strap, and he's got the mug in his other hand. Wyck's at eleven paces, straight up the slope, standing still. The mule's — the mule's further than I thought. The mule's at about twenty-six, and it's eating. Senna's in the cart, and she's sat up. Tor's at the tailgate, and he's turned round now. He's turned round because I said your name."
cues.reason: The mundane spatial report becomes evidence of a new ability.

cues.delivery: Rook protects her by giving procedure, not reassurance; make the promise firm and immediately return to the task.
cues.from: "That's exactly right, and it's the last time you'll ever have to do that on your own," said Rook. "Now stop talking about it for a minute. Sit there and think about the corn."
cues.through: "That's exactly right, and it's the last time you'll ever have to do that on your own," said Rook. "Now stop talking about it for a minute. Sit there and think about the corn."
cues.reason: His first response to her isolation is quietly consequential.

cues.delivery: Hold the waiting taut inside Toren’s body; do not anticipate the result or accelerate the silence.
cues.from: She sat with it for perhaps a minute and a half, which Toren, standing at the wheel, found almost unbearable.
cues.through: She sat with it for perhaps a minute and a half, which Toren, standing at the wheel, found almost unbearable.
cues.reason: The Reading’s uncertainty is almost physically unbearable to him.

cues.delivery: Name her new status with ceremonial weight held inside technical clarity; wonder belongs to recognition, never spectacle.
cues.from: "And it isn't going down because it's lit, not spent. That's the whole difference, and it's the one everybody has to be shown twice." He sat back on his heels. "Dessa Cole. That's Ember. That's the rank, and that's the word people will use about you now, and they'll be right, and I'd like you to hear the rest of it before anybody says anything else.
cues.through: "Kindled is a door standing open. Ember is the first thing that stays lit when you stop looking at it. He got there on a towpath with a sack of corn on his chest" — a nod at Toren — "and that one got there on a press-house step without noticing he'd done it, and you have got there sitting in wet grass on nineteen separate evenings getting nothing, which is the hardest of the three by a distance, and the other two should think about that."
cues.reason: Dessa’s identity and tactical rank fundamentally change here.

cues.delivery: Let disbelief thin the voice slightly as she fears the ability is too ordinary to count; no self-pity.
cues.from: "It's not a wall, and it's not a shape, and it's not a — it's just knowing where things are." Her voice went slightly. "That's not anything. That's not a thing you can show anybody. I've been doing that from a bank and a press-house step for a fortnight, and everybody thought I was being useful."
cues.through: "It's not a wall, and it's not a shape, and it's not a — it's just knowing where things are." Her voice went slightly. "That's not anything. That's not a thing you can show anybody. I've been doing that from a bank and a press-house step for a fortnight, and everybody thought I was being useful."
cues.reason: Dessa’s doubt threatens to undo the recognition she has just received.

cues.delivery: Answer her doubt with exact, seasoned certainty; Rook is granting durable worth, not offering comfort.
cues.from: "It's real, and it will be the most valuable thing in any party you ever stand in, and you will spend the whole of your life being told it isn't anything," said Rook, "by people whose stones make a noise. I told the one with the bar something like this on a press-house step eleven days ago, and I'll tell you the same, and then I'll stop.
cues.through: "A man who can put a shape on the end of his arm is worth having. A person who knows where all six of you are in the dark, all the time, without looking, is worth the whole of the rest of the party, and everybody finds that out at about four in the morning on the worst night of their lives."
cues.reason: He establishes the life-saving value of her seemingly invisible gift.

cues.delivery: Build through her audit toward quiet release: permission ended the checking. Keep the dead present as fact, not lament.
cues.from: "That's all it was. I've been sitting down every night for a fortnight trying to find out whether the four seconds belonged to me or to his stone or to the weather, and every single night the entire exercise was a girl auditing herself. And then last night a man told me I was the third person he's ever seen do it and that the other two are dead and that I am, personally, on my own, sitting on a stone with a bad leg, the proof of the thing she died holding on to." She turned the mug round. "And this morning I got up, and it was just — settled. It's mine. Somebody who'd know said so. And then there was nothing left to check, and I sat down at four o'clock to do the nothing, and I did the nothing properly for the first time in my life, and it took about a minute."
cues.through: "That's all it was. I've been sitting down every night for a fortnight trying to find out whether the four seconds belonged to me or to his stone or to the weather, and every single night the entire exercise was a girl auditing herself. And then last night a man told me I was the third person he's ever seen do it and that the other two are dead and that I am, personally, on my own, sitting on a stone with a bad leg, the proof of the thing she died holding on to." She turned the mug round. "And this morning I got up, and it was just — settled. It's mine. Somebody who'd know said so. And then there was nothing left to check, and I sat down at four o'clock to do the nothing, and I did the nothing properly for the first time in my life, and it took about a minute."
cues.reason: Dessa explains the inward surrender that allowed the ability to settle.

cues.delivery: Use Ott’s market-dry greeting and Milo’s proud announcement as a short, unforced release; keep Dessa’s correction quick.
cues.from: "Well," she said. "You're all still upright."
cues.through: "Two Ember," said Milo, "and one more since Tuesday," and Dessa hit him in the arm.
cues.reason: A restrained comic beat precedes the arrival of dangerous intelligence.

cues.delivery: Drop the information plainly and let possession in “your lot” carry the threat; no ominous flourish.
cues.from: "Your lot are at Barrow Gate."
cues.through: "Your lot are at Barrow Gate."
cues.reason: The distant enemy becomes a named, reachable presence.

cues.delivery: Slow around Toren’s helpless recognition; the danger is having to witness what this object will do to Rook.
cues.from: He did it slowly. He turned it over once in his fingers and held it out across the fire, flat on his palm, and Toren realised that he was going to have to watch this happen and that there was nothing whatsoever he could do about it.
cues.through: He did it slowly. He turned it over once in his fingers and held it out across the fire, flat on his palm, and Toren realised that he was going to have to watch this happen and that there was nothing whatsoever he could do about it.
cues.reason: The brass chit converts intelligence into a personal reckoning.

cues.delivery: Make the recruitment deadline sound like logistics closing a trap, with no villainous color.
cues.from: "And they break on the new moon," she said. "Everybody at that wall knows it because the yard's been hired to that date, and the weighmaster's counting the hours. They break, and they go, and nobody at Barrow Gate will know where, because they never do, and they've never once told anybody anything."
cues.through: "And they break on the new moon," she said. "Everybody at that wall knows it because the yard's been hired to that date, and the weighmaster's counting the hours. They break, and they go, and nobody at Barrow Gate will know where, because they never do, and they've never once told anybody anything."
cues.reason: The new moon gives the group only a narrow window.

cues.delivery: Rook exposes the column he normally conceals. Keep every number clean; resignation lives beneath the arithmetic, never over it.
cues.from: "And here's the other column, and I'd like everybody to watch me do it, because this is the bit I'd usually keep.
cues.through: "And she had a bad night four days ago. She'll have another one. I can hold a gate for a night, and I have got about" — he did not open the flask; he did not need to — "about two of those left in me and in what I'm carrying, and after that there's nothing between her and the road but the road."
cues.reason: The true cost of leaving is calculated in Senna’s remaining nights.

cues.delivery: Senna spends her breath on cold logic. Preserve her authority and dry edge; mortality is acknowledged without pleading or bravery.
cues.from: Senna said, from the cart, "Then go."
cues.through: "So go. And I'd like it minuted that the old woman said so first, and without anybody asking her, and that she was not being brave, she was doing sums."
cues.reason: She offers her own likely death as the rational price of Rook’s chance.

cues.delivery: State the odds with brutal tactical candor. The terror lies in four children left without protection, not in raised volume.
cues.from: "Forty men in a walled yard," said Rook. "I've been honest with you about everything else, so: I don't know what happens when I walk into that. I'd back myself at ten. I don't know about forty, and neither does anybody else, because nobody's ever tried it, because it's an idiotic thing to do.
cues.through: "I'm not doing it." He picked his coat up off the cart shaft. "And I want one thing understood, because Milo's face is doing something, and I'd rather kill it now. I'm not being noble. There isn't a noble version of this. What I am doing is choosing which of two things I want more, and I've chosen, and I'm going to be poor company about it for a while."
cues.reason: Rook reveals that the proposed six-day absence may be permanent.

cues.delivery: Let the cruel timing register through duration, the flat flask, and the transfer into Senna’s cup; resist elegy.
cues.from: They made three miles that afternoon and camped early, and Senna had her bad night a day sooner than anybody expected, which Toren afterward thought was the cruellest possible arrangement of the facts.
cues.through: Then he drank about half of what was in it, and poured the rest into Senna's cup — which is a thing Toren had never seen anybody do in his life and had not known was possible.
cues.reason: Senna’s collapse immediately exacts the cost Rook had just calculated.

cues.delivery: Make his final valuation absolute and unsentimental: possession becomes time for her, and the decision is already closed.
cues.from: "It's ash out of a road seam, and there's nine days of me in that flask, and I've just spent the lot," said Rook. "It buys her about four days of walking she wouldn't otherwise have, and it is the best use anything in my possession has ever been put to."
cues.through: "It's ash out of a road seam, and there's nine days of me in that flask, and I've just spent the lot," said Rook. "It buys her about four days of walking she wouldn't otherwise have, and it is the best use anything in my possession has ever been put to."
cues.reason: Rook confirms that he has spent his remaining magical reserve on Senna.

cues.delivery: Confess the unresolved cost quietly: certainty about the choice has not made the loss lie flat.
cues.from: "And I'd do it the same way tomorrow," he said, "and that's the part I can't get to sit down flat."
cues.through: "And I'd do it the same way tomorrow," he said, "and that's the part I can't get to sit down flat."
cues.reason: Rook names the contradiction he cannot reconcile.

cues.delivery: Toren offers a practical future rather than consolation; place modest conviction on the four-person line.
cues.from: "You'll get another one, and this time you'll have four people who can hold a line."
cues.through: "You'll get another one, and this time you'll have four people who can hold a line."
cues.reason: His reassurance reflects the responsibility Rook has transferred to them.
